newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI says in talks with Lonrho.
newsitem.headline: JCI says in talks with Lonrho.

text.p: JCI Ltd said on Monday it was in preliminary talks with British conglomerate Lonrho Plc and would issue a cautionary announcement to shareholders later in the day.
"JCI Ltd is in talks with Lonrho in respect of a possible merger," JCI spokesman Marc Gonsalves told Reuters.
Gonsalves said the company would not comment further given the nature of the discussions and would issue a cautionary anouncement to shareholders later on Monday.
"We would be issuing a cautionary this morning as well," he said.
Lonrho Plc said earlier on Monday that it has had preliminary talks with JCI to identify any benefits of combining the two groups.
But it said that it has not tabled or considered any merger proposals.
Lonrho and JCI were responding to newspaper reports that they were in merger talks in a move that would create one of the world's largest mining companies.

Britain's Sunday Telegraph said that under the proposals Lonrho would bid for JCI, which is valued at 900 million pounds ($1.5 billion), and the new company would be listed in London and Johannesburg.
The newspaper said the plan envisaged Anglo American Corporation of South Africa swapping its 28 percent stake in Lonrho, plus some cash, for Lonrho's 41 percent in Ghanaian gold mine Ashanti.
